systems/character-creation.html.title: Character Creation
systems/character-creation.html.description:
When creating a character, you will first choose from the list of playable races, which provide base values that your character will have in the main 3 stats: Primal, Mental, and Defense. In addition to these base values, you may choose one of these three main stats to allocate an extra point into. primalmentaldefenseAdditionally, you will mark down the limbs that your race provides. These limbs will determine what actions you can perform in combat, and your maximum vitality. Listed below are the remaining stats of the system apart from the main 3: Your expendable effort per combat round. Default effort value is 5 for all characters. A ratio of defensive effort to damage blocked. Your armor value is listed on your equipped armor. This stat is noted like asdef : dmg Vitality is your life-essence or health. Your character's vitality is capped by your Max Vitality, or "MV". Your maximum vitality represents how much life essence you can have. The "potential energy" of a living creature. Your MV is the sum of your limb's vitality values. Your attuned vitality is how much vitality your vessel is capable of containing without the adverse effects of vitality imbalance. Characters start with their attuned vitality equal to their max vitality. This grouping of Vitality stats can be noted as vit / max (attuned)
The story system keeps up with your character's life up to now, as well as what happens in each "Chapter" of the campaign. For character creation, simply choose a background and fill in your related stats. Feel free to flavor the background in any way you'd like, and bring up alternatives to the GM for alternative selections of skills.

systems/noncombat.html.title: Noncombat
systems/noncombat.html.description:
In noncombat, you will either be RPing, or passing larger chunks of time with "Downtime"During downtime, each player will state what they're doing by selecting a downtime action from below. These actions often apply the character's skills in any way applicable.Additionally, some scars may heal during downtime or resting, so check their descriptions. By training for 1 downtime period, you may increase your proficiency with a weapon, item, or limb. Cost: Reduce your vitality by your primal stat. story stufflist backgroundsList all skills here, and what type they are.
Then, make skill-checks of the highest type add that much proficiency (by the lead amount.)Ex:
Player has Physical as their strongest stat by 2pts => Physically proficient.

damage-types.html.title: damage types
damage-types.html.description:
Reduce your vitality by x damage. Reduce your maximum vitality by x damage.
( Your vitality must be less than or equal to this maximum. )Alternate between reducing your vitality and maximum vitality for each point of damage taken (always start with internal). Ex: 3 damage would be 1 external damage and 2 internal damage.

index.html.title: index
index.html.description:
New World ttrpg version 0.2.0 ( revision notes )
Character Creation
Noncombat
Combat The "New World" system is designed around the d6 for noncombat and skill-checks, however the full cast of dice is available to limb actions and weapons attacks. Players sit around the table in clockwise descending order of their character's Mental stat value. This allows the players taking their turn towards the end of a round to "play more reactively" to their comrade's actions.

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
